131740.overview:
The Lord of the Rings is a pinball game designed by George Gomez, and released by Stern Pinball in November 2003. It is based on the The Lord of the Rings (film series), which was first released in 2001. 

It features the highest possible score multiplier in pinball to date: During a combined "Two Towers" and "Gollum" Multiball it is possible to achieve a 84x Jackpot (when scoring seven subsequent combo Jackpot shots, having the 2x scoring Elf gift and the Sméagol phase of Gollum Multiball running at once). 

This game was re-released in December 2009 as The Lord of the Rings: Limited Edition, which adds a shaker motor and updated software.

A total of 5,100 units were produced.

178064.overview:
Lethal Weapon 3 is a licensed pinball table from Data East. It was designed by Joe Kaminkow and Ed Cebula, with artwork by Markus Rothkranz. The game was released in June 1992, just a month after the premiere of the third movie.

The game is somewhat misnamed, as it actually incorporates scenes and sound clips from the first three films. Hit the three LW saucers to complete various stunts like the High Fall, Joshua's helicopter, and Murtaugh's exploding toilet, then cap them off with the Super Stunt Spectacular. Alternately, shoot the outer loop to load bullets into the Uzi, then use it to shoot the villains on the display for various bonuses. Cut the correct wire to disarm the bomb, shoot the practice targets for Leo Getz, then loop the right orbit in the Getaway while Crazy Riggs racks up the score to the accompaniment of The Three Stooges. For even faster scoring, start the Lotsaballs multiball mode, then try to score the Speed, Double, and Quadruple Jackpots.

196224.overview: Lunelle is a rare solid-state pinball machine released around 1982 by Taito do Brasil, the Brazilian division of the Japanese company Taito. The game is widely known among enthusiasts for being a clone or heavily inspired by Williams' 1980 classic, Alien Poker.

460267.overview:
Taito do Brasil was known for adapting popular international pinball designs for the Brazilian market. Lady Luck is essentially a mirror-imaged version of Bally’s 1978 hit "Mata Hari". While the layout is nearly identical, the artwork was modified to fit the "Lady Luck" gambling and luck-based theme.

Key Features & Gameplay

• Magnetized Flippers: A standout feature of this machine is the inclusion of magnetic flippers, which was a common technological flourish in several Taito do Brasil tables.

• Playfield Mechanics: The table includes two magnets located under the drop targets that can be activated to influence ball movement.

• The "LADY" Lights: The game features a set of lights spelling out "LADY." In its sister table, "Vegas," players could change the order of these blinking lights, a feature added after feedback from the initial Lady Luck release.

462198.overview: The Lucky Strike pinball machine, released by Taito do Brasil in 1978, is a solid-state table known for its distinctive Brazilian flair and historical place in the South American arcade market. While it shares a name with earlier tables from Williams and Gottlieb, Taito's version is a unique production from their era as a major manufacturer in Brazil.

469426.overview:
Spin, bounce, and juice up your score! This fruity frenzy mixes classic slot machines vibes with fast pinball action.

Lucky Fruit is a classic electro-mechanical pinball machine released in 1975 by the Italian manufacturer Zaccaria. It is one of the company's early single-player models, produced shortly after their founding in 1974.

470403.overview: Released in 2018, The Last of Us is a Visual Pinball X table based on Naughty Dog's 2013 action-adventure video game. It is a re-theme of the JP Salas table "Pokemon Pinball".

471099.overview:
The Legend of Zelda is a homebrew digital pinball table that was created by LoadedWeapon in 2009 for Future Pinball, and years later ported over to Visual Pinball by JP Salas. 

The table itself is a re-theme of Roney Pinball's original Future Pinball table, "Medieval Castle".

472110.overview:
The Ultimate Edition of The Lord of the Rings pinball table for Future Pinball is a high-quality recreation of the 2003 Stern machine, known for its updated graphics, cinematic lighting, video clips, music and call-outs directly from the film trilogy.

Francisco666 was the first to recreate the table in Future Pinball; SLAMT1LT released his ULTIMATE Edition mod in 2015, and RLR released an updated version with FizX 3.3 physics in 2025.

478523.overview:
Los Jetsons by Roney Pinball is a Future Pinball table released in 2006. Based on the classic Hanna-Barbera futuristic cartoon, this original homebrew game features artwork and audio elements themed around George Jetson and family. The table uses a mix of Spanish and English for the in-game graphics.

A series of mods (versions 1.0 through 1.3) by PixelOz provides an extensive overhaul for Roney Pinball's original map. It implements antialiasing, smoother asset edges, cleaner geometry textures, and dedicated dual-language translations (complete Spanish and English graphic variants).

479942.overview:
Set in 1532, The Mysterious Cities of Gold follows Esteban, an 11-year-old orphan in Barcelona, Spain, who possesses a mysterious ability to summon the sun. Recruited by a navigator named Mendoza, Esteban joins an expedition to the New World to find his lost father and the fabled Seven Cities of Gold.

Originally screened in 1982–1983, and co-produced by French company DIC Entertainment and Japanese studio Pierrot, this animated historical fantasy adventure series serves as the theme for the Visual Pinball X table, "Les Mystérieuses Cités d'Or", a mod of Bally's 1979 table, Supersonic.

480154.overview:
Lesbian Pirates from Outer Space is an original table for Future Pinball inspired by Ro Salarian's "I Was Kidnapped By Lesbian Pirates from Outer Space" webcomic. The premise centers on Susan Bell, a secretary living in the 1950s who is kidnapped by a group of titular lesbian pirates, a race of Amazonesque beings who come from a planet referred to as "Lesbos-1."

The comic follows the humorous and occasionally risqué situations that develop as Susan lives alongside them, and chronicles Susan's eventual realization that she too is homosexual. The art style mimics 1950s pulp sci-fi magazines, complete with retro outfits, beehive hairdos, and ray guns.
